page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-8 is a graphics-optimized server instance designed for GPU-accelerated computing workloads. The system features 8 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs built on 4 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.2 GHz, with 2 threads per core. System memory totals 32 GB, yielding a balanced 4 GB of RAM per vCPU ratio. Cache architecture includes 32 KB L1d, 1 MB L2, and 38 MB L3 cache. The server includes no complimentary local storage, requiring external persistent disk attachments for data storage.

Hardware acceleration is supplied by a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture with 24 GB of total VRAM. Benchmark results show exceptional strength in machine learning inference, where the instance achieves top-tier performance for small (135M) and medium (7B) model prompt processing and text generation. Conversely, standard compute benchmarks show average multi-core CPU performance and low single-core execution speed, as reflected in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scores.

The g2-standard-8 configuration prioritizes GPU acceleration efficiency over raw single-threaded CPU processing. It offers an efficient platform for artificial intelligence inference, computer vision tasks, video processing, and general machine learning deployments that rely heavily on GPU parallel compute capabilities rather than heavy host CPU throughput.
description: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-8 is a graphics-optimized server instance built for GPU-accelerated tasks. It combines 8 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs (4 physical Intel Xeon cores at 2.2 GHz) and 32 GB of RAM with a single NVIDIA L4 GPU equipped with 24 GB of Ada Lovelace VRAM. The instance features no bundled local storage. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate top-tier performance in small and medium large language model inference tasks, alongside average multi-core CPU capacity and memory bandwidth. Single-core CPU computation ranks lower in benchmark testing. This server provides a cost-effective hardware footprint for AI inference, real-time video transcoding, computer vision, and graphic rendering applications.
